name: vtc-host
description: Verifiable Trust Community (VTC) service identity. Declares three keys: an Ed25519 signing key (#key-0), an X25519 key-agreement key (#key-1), and an ML-DSA-44 post-quantum signing key (#key-2). Both signing keys are assertion methods, so every credential this VTC issues carries a proof from each — a verifier that has not migrated checks the eddsa-jcs-2022 proof and one that has checks the mldsa44-jcs-2024 proof, neither needing to know about the other. The primary signing key is Ed25519 and cannot be otherwise: it signs the did:webvh log, and didwebvh 1.0 mandates eddsa-jcs-2022 for log-entry proofs. The post-quantum key falls back to ed25519 on a VTA that cannot mint ML-DSA, so one template serves a fleet mid-migration. Provisions the did:webvh that a vtc-service binary operates under. The document advertises the VTC's REST endpoint and the URL where its BitstringStatusList credentials will be hosted (populated in Phase 2 of the VTC MVP — the endpoint is gracefully present in the DID document from day one so external verifiers can pre-cache the resolution). Optionally advertises a TrustRegistry referral naming the registry authoritative for this community by DID, so a client holding only the community's DID can resolve one hop to its registry (TRQP v2 §'machine-discoverable via the authority_id'); supply SERVICE_TRUST_REGISTRY, built by vta_sdk::did_templates::referral_service, and omit it for a community with no registry. Messaging transports are chosen at setup and rendered here: supply SERVICE_TSP and/or SERVICE_DIDCOMM (built by vta_sdk::did_templates::tsp_service / didcomm_service) to advertise them, and omit either to prune it. Both name the SAME mediator DID — the transport URL lives in the mediator's own document. Decide this at mint: a VTC cannot re-sign its own log, so adding a transport later is a VTA-side `dids edit`, then, for a VTC serving its own did.jsonl, `cnm did-log install` with the extended log. Advertise both when you advertise either — the stack prefers TSP over DIDComm over REST, so a document offering TSP alone leaves every peer that does not speak TSP with no messaging route in. Advertising a transport the named mediator does not actually route produces an entry clients will choose and cannot use; the mediator's own services are its controller's responsibility and nothing here can verify them. Emitted service order is canonical (TSP, DIDComm, then REST). The URL variable must not end with a trailing slash to avoid double-slash artefacts in the status-list endpoint. REST_PATH is the API base the VTCRest entry advertises and defaults to /v1, which is what vtc-service actually serves — a bare {URL} answers 405 to every request a client derives from the document, and nothing in this workspace consumes that entry, so the only party who finds out is the third party trusting it. Set it to an empty string only for a deployment that serves the API at the root.
